name: Shebna the treasurer
charge: Hewing himself a sepulchre on high; a shame to his lord's house
summary: Over the house of the king in Hezekiah's day, Shebna cut himself a tomb in the rock as if Jerusalem were his to be buried in on high. Isaiah was sent to him with a sentence: the Lord would toss him like a ball into a large country and give his office to Eliakim.
offense: Shebna, who was over the house, prepared himself a sepulchre on high. Isaiah challenged what right he had to establish that memorial there (Isaiah 22:15-16). The officer entrusted with a household's affairs had directed his concern toward the permanence of his own name. The surrounding prophecy describes a city attending to walls and water while failing to look to its Maker (Isaiah 22:9-11). Shebna's monument belonged to that misplaced confidence. A carved habitation in the rock could not secure the future of the man who built it.
judgment: Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee. He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord's house. And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down. The key of the house of David was laid on the shoulder of Eliakim the son of Hilkiah instead. By the time Rabshakeh came, Shebna was already only the scribe.

entries.commentary: The burden of the valley of vision falls on a city gone up to the housetops, a tumultuous and once joyous city whose slain men are not slain with the sword nor dead in battle. Its rulers are fled together and bound, and the prophet turns away to weep bitterly and will not be comforted.

It is a day of trouble, of treading down, and of perplexity by the Most High of hosts in the valley of vision, with the walls broken down and a crying to the mountains. Elam bears the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield, so the choicest valleys are full of chariots set in array at the gate.

The people look to their defenses in that day: the breaches of the city of David, the gathering of the waters of the lower pool, the numbering and breaking down of houses to fortify the wall, and a ditch made between the two walls for the water of the old pool. Yet they have not looked unto the Maker thereof nor had respect unto Him that fashioned it long ago.

In that day the Most High of hosts calls to weeping, mourning, baldness, and girding with sackcloth, but instead there is joy and gladness, slaying oxen and eating flesh, saying "let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die." The Most High reveals that this iniquity shall not be purged from them till they die.

The word comes against Shebna, the treasurer over the house, who has hewn himself out a sepulchre on high and graved a habitation for himself in a rock. The Most High will carry him away with a mighty captivity, toss him like a ball into a large country where he shall die, and drive him from his station and pull him down from his state.

In Shebna's place the Most High calls His servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, clothing him with the robe and girdle and committing the government into his hand, so he is a father to Jerusalem and to Judah with the key of the house of David laid upon his shoulder to open and shut. He is fastened as a nail in a sure place for a glorious throne, yet in that day the nail shall be removed, cut down, and fall, and the burden upon it cut off.

Hezekiah son of Ahaz begins to reign over Judah in the third year of Hoshea, the last king of Israel before the captivity. He does that which is right according to all that David his father did, removing the high places, breaking the images, and cutting down the groves. He breaks in pieces the brazen serpent Moses made in the wilderness, which had stood from that time and was now being burned incense to, and he calls it Nehushtan.

Hezekiah trusts in the Most High so that none among the kings of Judah, before or after, was like him. He clave to the Most High, kept the commandments, and the Most High was with him so that he prospered. Prospering here does not mean a mansion or luxury, but the blessing that comes from keeping and doing the commandments. He rebels against the king of Assyria and smites the Philistines even unto Gaza. -

In Hezekiah's fourth year Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, and after three years, in Hezekiah's sixth year, Samaria is taken. Israel was not removed all at once but carried away in stages into Assyria. The reason given again is that they obeyed not the voice of the Most High but transgressed His covenant and all Moses commanded. -

Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against the fenced cities of Judah and takes them. Hezekiah sends to Lakish acknowledging offense and agrees to bear whatever tribute is laid on him. Assyria appoints three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold, so Hezekiah gives all the silver of the house of the Most High and even cuts the gold from the temple doors.

The king of Assyria sends Tartan, Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh with a great host to Jerusalem, and they stand by the conduit of the upper pool. Rabshakeh challenges Hezekiah's confidence, mocking his trust and calling Egypt a bruised reed that pierces the hand of any who lean on it. He argues that because Hezekiah removed the high places, even Judah's own worship is now confined to one altar, twisting the reform into a weakness. He boasts that Assyria came up against the land by the word of the Most High Himself, claiming divine backing to destroy it.

Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall will not understand, but he refuses. Rabshakeh cries aloud in the Jews' language, warning the people not to let Hezekiah deceive them or make them trust in the Most High. He promises the people their own vines, fig trees, and waters if they surrender, then a land like their own, seeking to turn them from their king. He asks whether the gods of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah delivered their lands, claiming no god can deliver Jerusalem out of his hand. The people hold their peace and answer not a word, for Hezekiah had commanded silence. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah come to Hezekiah with their clothes rent and tell him the words of Rabshakeh. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)
Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. There is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.

Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. Fear him which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell. Not one sparrow is forgotten before God, and even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Things happen to a man that no one else sees; they are not unseen.

Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God. Unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven. When they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, for the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.

A man asks him to make his brother divide the inheritance, and is answered, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you? Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth. He discerned the thoughts of both men in that dispute. The rich man pulls down his barns to build greater, and is told, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee. So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, and God feedeth them. Consider the lilies: Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. After all these things do the nations of the world seek: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things. But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.

Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. Provide yourselves treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning, and be like men that wait for their lord. Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching. Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.

The faithful and wise steward gives the household their portion of meat in due season, and is made ruler over all his lord hath. The servant that says in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming, and begins to beat the menservants, has his portion appointed with the unbelievers. That servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, shall be beaten with many stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.
I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished. He was in anguish of mind over it. He knew what he had come to do.

Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division. The division named here is inside a house: father against son, mother against daughter, mother in law against daughter in law. Coming into this truth is where that starts.

Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky and of the earth; but how is it that ye do not discern this time? Men who can read the weather and every other sign will not read the one in front of them. Agree with thine adversary in the way, lest he hale thee to the judge, and thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God of hosts, Go, get thee unto this treasurer, even unto Shebna, which is over the house, and say,
What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high, and that graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?
Behold, the Lord will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee.
He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord’s house.
And I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down.
And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah:

And I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand: and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.
And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups, even to all the vessels of flagons.

In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall the nail that is fastened in the sure place be removed, and be cut down, and fall; and the burden that was upon it shall be cut off: for the Lord hath spoken it.
And when they had called to the king, there came out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, which was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder.
Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:
And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?
And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.
And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.
But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?
So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.
